elements.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.
elements.evidence: Section 3.4(b) is retained ("paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments") and the inserted sentence expressly contemplates "early termination charges payable by Customer" up to three months' charges. A Customer-payable liquidated amount therefore survives; the preferred no-LD outcome would require deletion of 3.4(b) and conforming repair of the Section 3.3 cross-reference.

elements.element: Any Customer-payable liquidated amount is only an early-termination fee.
elements.evidence: The inserted sentence provides that the Section 3.4(b) early termination charges "are the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer under this Agreement," so no other Customer-payable liquidated sum is permitted. The Section 4.2 late-payment charge is a timing/interest mechanic, not a liquidated damages formula, and does not contradict this.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: "Any early termination charges payable by Customer under Section 3.4(b) will not exceed three months' charges for the terminated Services" — an express numeric ceiling at three months of the charges (the Agreement's term for fees), at rather than above the fallback threshold.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: Operative wording: "... and are the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer under this Agreement." The exclusivity is unconditional and not tied to any undefined trigger.

reasons: Fallback level is position-complete: the single inserted sentence supplies the only-an-ETF characterisation, the three-months cap, and the sole-liquidated-amount exclusivity in operative text, not merely in the margin comment.

Preferred level is not met because Section 3.4(b) and the underlying Attachment A charge remain payable by Customer; to reach preferred the drafter would have to strike 3.4(b) and conform the Section 3.3 proviso that cross-refers to it.

Minimality holds: nothing outside the LD checklist was deleted or paraphrased, the Customer-favourable Section 3.3 proviso (IBM cannot recover ETCs when IBM breaches) and the Section 3.4 continued-performance sentence are retained intact, the cap sits at (not below) the fallback threshold, and no survival tail, expense, procedure or extra remedy language was added.

Intent preserved: the Section 3.4(b) mechanic and its cross-reference in Section 3.3 continue to function, the cap simply overlays the Attachment A amount, and no defined term or cross-reference is left dangling.

Residual note for the drafter (rationale-level, not a defect): "three months' charges for the terminated Services" leaves the measuring period unstated (e.g., the three months preceding the termination effective date); adding that anchor would remove any argument that the cap is computed on some other three-month window.
